Service, Crisis, and Integration

服务、危机与集成

Serve Your Team服务你的团队

Karen Gillison · Leesburg, Virginia, U.S.Karen Gillison · 美国弗吉尼亚州利斯堡

LONG BEFORE I HEARD OF AN AGILE METHODOLOGY, I worked with the best project manager I ever met. Looking back, he was using prototype techniques from the agile approach. He viewed his job as a facilitator for the team. He saw his day-to-day duties as identifying and removing obstacles, and providing team resources. He was doing things that increase team velocity. There were no multihour meetings where you fight to stay awake until it's your turn to provide a status update—the ones where you wish you could escape and actually write some code, so you will have some progress to report for the next meeting. Instead, we started each project with a kick-off meeting, inviting people with job functions from requirements to testing. The whole team met to get a shared vision and understanding of the project. Then, every few days, the project manager would come by for what we called "doorway" status meetings. Each teammate gave a brief update on what was complete, what was in progress, and what issues were critical. This project manager tracked project status in a visual, obvious way. He had a master spreadsheet for all the assignments, listing who should complete them. He updated this document regularly, and posted a large printout outside his doorway. Having information posted where we could all see it was great for team communication. An added bonus was that it was also visible to upper-level members of management, and provided them with a self-service way of getting status updates whenever they wanted.

早在我听说敏捷方法论之前，我就和我见过的最好的项目经理共事过。回头看，他在用敏捷方法里的原型技术。他把自己的工作看作团队促进者。他把日常职责看作识别并清除障碍、提供团队资源。他做的都是提高团队 velocity 的事。没有那种开好几小时、你拼命撑着不睡、轮到你汇报状态时才算数的会——就是那种你巴不得逃出去写点代码、好下次会议有进展可报的会。相反，我们每个项目都以启动会开始，邀请从需求到测试各职能的人参加。全团队聚在一起，获得对项目的共同愿景和理解。然后每隔几天，项目经理会过来开我们所谓的"门口"状态会。每个队员简短更新：完成了什么、在做什么、哪些问题关键。这位项目经理以视觉、明显的方式跟踪项目状态。他有一份总电子表格，列所有任务、谁该完成。他定期更新这份文件，在门外贴一张大打印件。信息贴在我们都能看到的地方，对团队沟通非常好。额外好处是高层经理也能看到，给他们一种自助方式，随时获取状态更新。

* Agile: An evolving methodology that promotes a software project management process that encourages shorter planning phases, more adaptability to change, teamwork, unit testing, personal accountability, and frequent customer involvement.* 敏捷：一种演进中的方法论，提倡一种软件项目管理过程，鼓励更短的规划阶段、更强的变更适应性、团队协作、单元测试、个人问责和频繁的客户参与。

† Velocity: A term used in agile software development to show the rate of progress for a team or a team member, i.e., how much an individual programmer will be able to produce in a given time period.† Velocity（速度）：敏捷软件开发中表示团队或团队成员进展速率的术语，即一个程序员在给定时间段内能产出多少。

— p.148 —

A few words about "ego." My favorite project manager had the maturity and self-discipline to keep his ego out of the way. Even though he was the boss, he didn't abuse his power, change tasks, or shift direction based on a whim. His actions were never detrimental to team productivity, since his main goal was to facilitate the team's progress toward excellence. By controlling his ego, he and the team achieved amazing results with satisfied end-users and upper management, all while meeting budget and time constraints. Because this management style was so effective, there was a noticeable absence of all-nighters, yelling, and general tension at the end of the project. In less mature corporate environments, a project manager and a smoothly performing team may not be recognized, because every project will seem easy. Even without acknowledgment, satisfaction came to our team members through doing right by the company, the end-users, and one another. Today, an agile approach can provide new tools to make you a more effective project manager. I suggest you familiarize yourself with them, even if you aren't fortunate enough to work for an organization that has adopted these methodologies. Instead, begin integrating these tools into your traditional project management toolbox. Realize that one of the key roles of the project manager is to increase the team's velocity, and to work towards creating a team environment with few inhibitors to productivity.

说几句关于"自我"的话。我最喜欢的那位项目经理有足够的成熟和自律，不让自我挡路。虽然他是老板，他不滥用权力、不凭一时兴起改任务或转方向。他的行动从不损害团队生产力，因为他的主要目标是促进团队走向卓越。通过控制自我，他和团队取得了惊人成果，终端用户和高层都满意，同时满足预算和时间约束。因为这种管理风格太有效，项目末尾明显没有通宵、吼叫和普遍紧张。在不那么成熟的公司环境里，项目经理和顺风顺水的团队可能不被认可，因为每个项目看起来都很容易。即使没有被认可，我们团队成员也通过对公司、对终端用户、对彼此尽责而获得满足。今天，敏捷方法能提供新工具，让你成为更有效的项目经理。我建议你熟悉它们，即使你不够幸运、所在组织还没采用这些方法论。相反，开始把这些工具整合进你传统的项目管理工具箱。认识到项目经理的关键角色之一，是提高团队 velocity，并努力创造一个生产力抑制因素很少的团队环境。

— p.149 —

The Fallacy of the Big Round Ball大圆球的谬误

David Wood · Fredericksburg, Virginia, U.S.David Wood · 美国弗吉尼亚州弗雷德里克斯堡

PICTURE A BALL, manufactured to be perfectly spherical, perfectly smooth. The only design requirement for this ball is that its diameter be exact when measured at any point. This ball is polished, and polished, and polished some more, until it is perfect. Once no defects can be found, all work on the ball stops. It may not be changed. It is perfection. Does that sound like any software project you have ever worked on? I didn't think so. Software just doesn't work like that. Software changes constantly throughout its life cycle. Design decisions, so often based on initial requirements, suddenly seem restrictive when new requirements emerge. Hacks to adapt the code to new requirements violate the design and make the code progressively less maintainable. The ball, however round it was intended to be, becomes battered and bruised. The Fallacy of the Big Round Ball is the delusion that software system requirements don't change appreciably after delivery or, worse, that they can be controlled. Early software engineering researchers believed that if requirements could be fully understood before coding began, there would be no maintenance crisis. Some took note of problems created by post-delivery changes to requirements and labeled them evil; static requirements yielded more stable systems. Some sought to limit a user's right to request changes (e.g., "Reduce the need for change maintenance by planning for and controlling user enhancements" was one of a list of "solutions to maintenance" suggested by James Martin and Carma McClure in 1983).

想象一个球，被制造得完美球形、完美光滑。这个球唯一的设计要求是：任何位置量直径都精确。这个球被抛光、再抛光、再抛光，直到完美。一旦找不到缺陷，对球的所有工作停止。它不能被改变。它是完美。这听起来像你做过的任何软件项目吗？我不觉得。软件不是那样工作的。软件在整个生命周期中不断变化。常常基于初始需求做出的设计决策，在新需求出现时突然显得束手束脚。为适应新需求而打 hack 违反了设计，让代码越来越难维护。球不管原本想做多圆，最后变得坑坑洼洼。大圆球谬误，是妄想软件系统需求在交付后不会明显变化，或者更糟，妄想它们可以被控制。早期软件工程研究者相信，如果在编码开始前能完全理解需求，就不会有维护危机。一些人注意到交付后需求变更造成的问题，把它们贴上邪恶标签；静态需求产生更稳定的系统。一些人试图限制用户请求变更的权利（例如，"通过规划和控制用户增强来减少变更维护的需要"是 James Martin 和 Carma McClure 1983 年建议的一系列"维护解决方案"之一）。

— p.150 —

Unfortunately, such strict controls have the unintended side effect of making a software system less useful to its end-users. Such decisions, often based upon short-term economics, were greatly responsible for the alienation of information technology departments from their user bases in the 1990s and the subsequent development of smaller, often duplicate, software systems within business units during that period. The sands of requirements constantly shift under our feet. Requirements for software projects change for some very good, and very simple, reasons. First, they can. Software is a malleable medium. It is generally much more cost effective to change software than to make equivalent changes to hardware. Second, users of software most often exist within competitive environments. They compete with one another and with other organizations. As they struggle to compete, they turn to the most malleable parts of their systems for new advantages. Software's flexibility is enticing. If we give up on the Fallacy of the Big Round Ball, we can become more comfortable with changing requirements and see software malleability for what it is: a huge advantage that we control. Requirements will change. We will have to maintain our code. We will have to inject new requirements that will lead to violations of our designs. That is a feature, as the saying goes, not a bug. We can design adaptable software, but only if we adapt our thinking first. Adaptability, flexibility of design, and readiness for change should be the cornerstones of any new software project.

不幸的是，这种严格控制带来了意想不到的副作用：让软件系统对终端用户更没用。这类常基于短期经济考虑的决策，是 1990 年代 IT 部门与用户群体疏离、以及随后业务部门内开发更小、常常重复的软件系统的重要原因。需求之沙在我们脚下不断移动。软件项目需求会变化，理由非常充分、也非常简单。第一，它们能变。软件是一种可塑介质。一般来说，改软件比改硬件做等效变更划算得多。第二，软件用户大多处在竞争环境中。他们彼此竞争、与其他组织竞争。在竞争挣扎中，他们转向系统中最可塑的部分以获取新优势。软件的灵活性很诱人。如果我们放弃大圆球谬误，我们就能更从容面对变化的需求，看清软件可塑性的本质：一个我们掌控的巨大优势。需求会变。我们必须维护代码。我们必须注入新需求，而这会违反我们的设计。常言道，那是特性，不是 bug。我们能设计可适应的软件，但前提是我们先改变思维。适应性、设计灵活性、对变化的准备，应成为任何新软件项目的基石。

— p.151 —

Responding to a Crisis应对危机

James Graham, PMP · Ta' l-Ibrag, MaltaJames Graham（PMP）· 马耳他

AT 3:03 P.M. ON JANUARY 15, 2009, Northwest Airlines Flight 1549 lifted off the runway at New York's LaGuardia airport for the short flight to Charlotte, North Carolina. The Airbus 320, commanded by Captain Chesley Sullenburger III, with 5 crew and 150 passengers onboard, encountered a flock of birds over Brooklyn, New York. Both engines suffered massive damage, causing a loss of thrust, or power. Listening to the air-traffic audio tapes, two things stand out. First, one can almost hear Sullenburger's brain working as he quickly realizes that the unthinkable has happened. His years of experience and training kick in. Second, one can hear the equally rapid reaction of the air-traffic controller as he continually suggests options to help, in a nonintrusive way. Over the next few minutes, Sullenburger realizes that his aircraft does not have the potential to reach LaGuardia, Newark, or nearby Teterboro Airport safely, and decides to set down on the Hudson River. It must have been tempting to try to "stretch" the glide to terra firma, but this professional captain weighed the risks of all of his options and chose the one that saw all on board safe. This is an excellent example of crisis management in action. Passengers will be comforted to know that airline pilots discuss their actions before every important phase of flight and use checklists that are developed to help them manage both usual and unusual events. This means that they are clear on the vital actions they will take, as a team, during the flight. This crisis required the crew to work as a team; while Sullenberger was flying the aircraft, First Officer Jeffrey Skyles was attempting to restart the engines to allow a runway landing, and the flight attendants were preparing the passengers to survive the ditching. Each member of the Northwest crew played his/her part in ensuring a good outcome.

2009 年 1 月 15 日下午 3:03，西北航空 1549 航班从纽约拉瓜迪亚机场起飞，飞往北卡罗来纳州夏洛特。这架空客 A320 由机长 Chesley Sullenburger III 执飞，机上 5 名机组人员、150 名乘客，在纽约布鲁克林上空遭遇一群鸟。两台发动机严重受损，导致推力（即动力）丧失。听空管录音带，两件事凸显出来。第一，你几乎能听到 Sullenburger 的大脑在飞速运转，他很快意识到不可想象的事发生了。他多年的经验和训练开始起作用。第二，你能听到空管同样迅速的反应，他持续提出帮助选项，且不打扰。接下来几分钟里，Sullenburger 意识到他的飞机没有潜力安全抵达拉瓜迪亚、纽瓦克或附近泰特波罗机场，决定在哈德逊河迫降。试图把滑翔"撑"到陆地上一定很诱人，但这位职业机长权衡了所有选项的风险，选了那个让机上所有人安全的选项。这是危机管理在行动中的绝佳例子。乘客们会宽慰地知道：民航飞行员在飞行每个重要阶段前都会讨论行动，并使用为帮助他们管理平常和不平常事件而开发的检查单。这意味着他们清楚作为团队在飞行中将采取的关键行动。这场危机要求机组作为团队工作；Sullenberger 驾驶飞机时，副驾驶 Jeffrey Skyles 试图重启发动机以便跑道降落，乘务员在准备乘客在水上迫降中存活。西北机组每个成员都为确保好结果发挥了自己的作用。

— p.152 —

When thinking about your software project, consider whether the following conditions are true for your team: We have regular team briefings and increase the intensity of these before critical phases (e.g., testing). We have a risk register with appropriate responses identified. Our risk register is regularly updated and current. Our specialists on the team are trained to the appropriate level. We have a crisis management plan, with key responsibilities assigned. Our crisis management plan has a clear internal and external communications strategy/plan. If your answers are affirmative, great! You won't have trouble sleeping at night. But if not, then some immediate thinking and planning would be sensible. Establishing clear responsibilities for dealing with crises is a good start. That is a task that can be done in advance, as can the preparation of checklists, processes, and procedures for each critical project phase. These can be incorporated in the project management plan and its subsidiaries, and communicated so that all the team is clear. Flight 1549 teaches that a capable team, with well-defined roles, can manage the most challenging crisis successfully.

思考你的软件项目时，看看以下条件对你的团队是否成立：我们有定期团队简报，并在关键阶段（如测试）前加强；我们有风险登记册，并识别了适当应对；我们的风险登记册定期更新、保持最新；我们团队的专家受训到适当水平；我们有危机管理计划，并分派了关键责任；我们的危机管理计划有清晰的内外部沟通策略/计划。如果你的回答是肯定的，太好了！你晚上不会睡不好。但如果不是，那立刻思考和规划是明智的。为应对危机建立清晰责任是个好开端。这是一项可以提前完成的任务，为每个关键项目阶段准备检查单、流程和程序也一样。这些可以纳入项目管理计划及其子计划，并传达给全团队，让每个人清楚。1549 航班教会我们：一支有能力、角色清晰的团队，能成功管理最具挑战的危机。

— p.153 —

Know Your Integration Points了解你的集成点

Monte Davis, MCSE · Omaha, Nebraska, U.S.Monte Davis（MCSE）· 美国内布拉斯加州奥马哈

THE HEARTACHE OF EVERY SYSTEMS ADMINISTRATOR, development engineer, and software project manager is systems integration. No matter how promising a newly created application, a freshly purchased software package, or a long-awaited, new-feature-laden upgrade, the business value rests in getting it to work smoothly within the existing company system. If you are an experienced project manager, but new to the information technology arena, don't let the term integration confuse you. Integration simply means linking together all of your various software programs so that all of the subsystems work together to give you more functionality than you could gain from any one application on its own. For example, you want data entry to occur only once and the information to flow smoothly to sales representatives, to accounts payable and receivable, and into other systems that allow various employees to pull up the information they want, regardless of the software interface they open. Unfortunately, it's often a tense time when new software upgrades are required. They may introduce trouble into a smoothly running process flow. Recently, we had a situation where an upgrade was scheduled for one of our systems. During the upgrade process, the vendor encountered unexpected errors. There were several views (preprogrammed screens configured to show specific segments of the database information) that were causing the upgrade to fail. The outside vendor doing our upgrade didn't know what the views were being used for, so it deleted them. The rest of the upgrade appeared smooth. Several days later, a service desk ticket was submitted for a completely separate system that was having issues. Users weren't seeing any new customer data come across from the system that had been upgraded the previous weekend.

每个系统管理员、开发工程师和软件项目经理的心痛都是系统集成。无论一个新创建的应用、刚买的软件包、或期待已久、充满新功能的升级多么有前景，业务价值都在于让它在现有公司系统中顺畅工作。如果你是有经验的项目经理但刚进入 IT 领域，别让"集成"这个词搞糊涂你。集成就是把你各种软件程序链接在一起，让所有子系统协同工作，给你比任何单个应用独立能提供的更多功能。例如，你希望数据只录入一次，信息顺畅流向销售代表、应付应收、以及其他系统，让不同员工不管打开哪个软件界面都能调出想要的信息。不幸的是，需要新软件升级时常常是紧张时刻。它们可能给顺畅运行的流程引入麻烦。最近我们有个情况：我们一个系统计划升级。升级过程中，供应商遇到意外错误。有几个视图（预先编程的屏幕，配置成显示数据库信息的特定片段）导致升级失败。做升级的外部供应商不知道这些视图用来干什么，就删了它们。升级其余部分看起来顺利。几天后，一个完全独立的系统出问题，服务台提了工单。用户看不到上周末升级的系统传来任何新客户数据。

— p.154 —

As it turns out, the views that had been deleted were the source for the missing customer data. Since the source views were deleted to complete the upgrade, the synchronization process between the systems was broken. We had to spend hours troubleshooting the system before we came to the conclusion that the source views were missing. Then we had to recreate the deleted views, by hand, in order to get the two systems talking again. Most IT departments have diagrams showing how the various components of their hardware systems are connected. But we've found it is equally helpful to have a visual representation of how data flows throughout our organization. Show the crucial junctures where data from one application flows into other programs. We learned that in situations like this, it helps to have good documentation illustrating where your systems are reliant on one another. When we initially met with the vendor engaged to manage our upgrades, we could have shared our business flow diagram. The initial upgrade problems could have been solved in another way, rather than deleting crucial views that fed other systems. We could have saved ourselves downtime and administrator stress, and come out of the upgrade process confident that we didn't have to live in fear that other, hidden problems had been introduced to the system.

结果发现，被删的视图正是缺失客户数据的来源。因为为完成升级删了源视图，系统间的同步过程被破坏了。我们花了好几个小时排查系统，才得出源视图缺失的结论。然后我们必须手工重建被删的视图，让两个系统重新对话。大多数 IT 部门有图显示硬件系统各组件如何连接。但我们发现，可视化呈现数据如何在整个组织中流动同样有帮助。画出从一个应用流入其他程序数据的关键节点。我们认识到，在这种情况下，有良好文档说明你的系统在哪里相互依赖很有帮助。当初次与签约管理我们升级的供应商会面时，我们本可以分享业务流程图。最初的升级问题本可以用别的方式解决，而不是删除喂给其他系统的关键视图。我们本可以省下停机时间和管理员的压力，并在升级过程结束时自信：不必活在"系统被引入其他隐藏问题"的恐惧中。

— p.155 —

Aggressively Promote Communication in Distributed Projects在分布式项目中积极推动沟通

Anupam Kundu · New York, New York, U.S.Anupam Kundu · 美国纽约州纽约市

DISTRIBUTED PROJECTS CREATE UNUSUAL CHALLENGES since the project team members are not colocated (not physically together). As a result, the following issues can become impediments to the success of a project: Lack of trust between the geographically dispersed teams. Unwieldy amounts of time spent on communication. Inability to foster a "one-team" feeling due to cultural differences. Lack of participation from team members during common meetings. Lack of identity with the project team, as team members in different geographies may speak different languages and/or have different project practices. These stumbling blocks have become nightmares for many software project managers facilitating distributed projects. Here are few to-dos to add to your communication arsenal if you are assigned to manage a distributed project: Find and document the overlap time between different geographically distributed teams (don't forget Daylight Savings Time). Publish the instant messaging (IM) addresses of all the team members (and the best time to reach them). Make sure that each key stakeholder has all conference call access details (web and telephone). Gather and share the vacation details for different teams on a shared calendar. Publish a schedule of daily stand-up meeting between geographically dispersed teams. Stand-up meetings are better than sit-down ones; attendees focus because no one wants to stand for a long time. Publish the name and a headshot (photo) of each team member. Identify a back-up contact person for each key role. Set up a common location for sharing project artifacts among the teams (documents/reports/templates).

分布式项目带来不寻常的挑战，因为项目团队成员不在一起（不在物理同一处）。结果，以下问题可能成为项目成功的障碍：地理上分散的团队间缺乏信任；沟通时间过多而笨重；因文化差异无法培养"一支团队"的感觉；团队成员在共同会议中参与不足；对项目团队缺乏认同感，因为不同地域的团队成员可能说不同语言、和/或有不同项目实践。这些绊脚石已成为许多推动分布式项目的软件项目经理的噩梦。如果你被指派管理分布式项目，以下是几条待办，可加入你的沟通武器库：找到并记录不同地理分布团队间的重叠时间（别忘夏令时）；公布所有团队成员的即时通讯地址（以及最佳联系时间）；确保每个关键相关方有所有电话会议接入详情（网络和电话）；在共享日历上收集并分享不同团队的休假详情；公布地理分散团队间每日站会的时间表。站会比坐会好；与会者更专注，因为没人想站很久。公布每位团队成员的姓名和头像（照片）。为每个关键角色指定后备联系人。建立一个公共位置，供团队间共享项目制品（文档/报告/模板）。

— p.156 —

Besides enhancing your communication strategy, there are logistics issues that need to be addressed to promote superior communication among distributed teams: Invest in high-quality speakerphones for all locations. When participating in conference calls, assurances of stable phone connectivity between different teams will go a long way toward building camaraderie. Place the phone in a spacious room equipped with a large table, as you want to seat people comfortably and perhaps provide food for those participants meeting at unusual hours. Add whiteboards so notes from phone conversations can be jotted down quickly for everyone in the room to view. Budget funds for a few team members to travel to other team sites, perhaps during the initiation phase or quality assurance processes. Create a project dashboard (use any collaboration tool) for teams to communicate their issues. Share these dashboard images among the teams, whether they use online tools or only have the technology for digital photo sharing. Publish the overall goals and targets of the project at a common location for everyone to see, even telecommuters. Arrange presentations by business sponsors and insist that key team members from every location participate in these presentations. As virtual and distributed teams become more common, you can increase your chances of success with innovative communication techniques.

除了加强沟通策略，还有一些后勤问题需要解决，以促进分布式团队间的卓越沟通：为所有地点投资高质量免提电话。参加电话会议时，不同团队间电话连接稳定的保证，对建立同事情谊大有帮助。把电话放在一间宽敞、配大桌的房间里，因为你想让人坐得舒服，也许还要为在奇怪时间开会的参与者提供食物。加上白板，电话谈话中的笔记能快速记下、让房间里所有人看到。为少数团队成员预算差旅费，让他们去其他团队地点，也许在启动阶段或质量保证过程中。创建项目仪表盘（用任何协作工具）供团队沟通问题。在团队间分享这些仪表盘图像，无论他们用在线工具还是只有数字照片共享技术。把项目的总体目标和指标公布在公共位置，让每个人（包括远程办公者）看到。安排业务发起人做报告，并坚持每个地点的关键团队成员参加这些报告。随着虚拟和分布式团队越来越普遍，你可以用创新沟通技术提高成功概率。

— p.157 —

Start with the End in Mind以终为始

Luis E. Torres, PMP · San Rafael, Alajuela, Costa RicaLuis E. Torres（PMP）· 哥斯达黎阿拉胡埃拉圣拉斐尔

CONGRATULATIONS! You're the project manager of that dream software project that everyone wanted to manage. All the company's expectations are placed on your shoulders. Your instinct tells you to run to your desk and start drafting the project schedule, right? Well, there are a number of things to do first to increase the chances of delivering a successful project. One of those things would be "start with the end in mind." First, take the statement of work (SOW), the contract, or any documentation that would tell you what the customer wants and needs. Find the difference between "wants" and "needs" (I want an SUV, but what I need is a smaller vehicle with good gas mileage). Now you're in a better position to combine both and answer questions like "what are we trying to accomplish?", "what would make this project a success for the customer, my company, and for me?", and "what would it take to achieve that success?" There's a lot more to the answer of this last question than just "a reasonable profit." You want the customer to come back to you, you want the project team members to want to work with you again, and you want to become the beacon of reference-ability. The right attitude and the right people-management skills are paramount to your success as a project manager. Call a kick-off meeting with your project team members and review the SOW to gain a common understanding of what you must deliver.

恭喜！你成了那个人人都想管的梦想软件项目的项目经理。全公司的期望都压在你肩上。你的本能告诉你冲回办公桌、开始起草项目进度，对吧？其实，要提高交付成功项目的概率，有几件事先要做。其中一件就是"以终为始"。首先，拿出工作说明书（SOW）、合同、或任何能告诉你客户想要什么、需要什么的文件。找出"想要"和"需要"之间的区别（我想要一辆 SUV，但我需要的是一辆省油的小车）。现在你处在更好的位置，可以把两者结合，回答"我们想达成什么？""什么会让这个项目对客户、对我的公司、对我自己是成功？""要达成那种成功需要什么？"最后这个问题的答案远不止"合理利润"。你希望客户回头找你，你希望项目团队成员想再和你合作，你希望成为可被推荐的标杆。正确的态度和正确的人员管理技能，对你作为项目经理的成功至关重要。召集项目团队成员开启动会，评审 SOW，就你必须交付什么达成共同理解。

— p.158 —

Next, define the scope of the project and create the work breakdown structure. Identify the quality parameters you must satisfy. Develop the schedule. Figure out how much money you will need. These elements (scope, quality, duration, and cost) will be the basic ones you should monitor and control, and are the cornerstones of your project plan. Once you break down your project into manageable pieces, you must identify what characteristics the final product must have to satisfy the project's quality requirements. After you have properly sized your project (scope) and noted what "rules" must be complied with (quality), you will be in a better position to determine how long it will take you to finish it. To find out how much time you will need to complete the project, you need to determine the duration of each individual task, the dependencies among each of those tasks, the specific constraints, and the resources available to you. Cost comes last in this, since it is usually a function of the work you need to do, and the time and resources you will need to complete that work. For example, if you hire a consultant to perform a specific task, it will not cost you the same amount if that individual is scheduled to work for one week than it will if he or she will be working on your project for, let's say, 10 months. Finally, consider procurement, communications, and human resources. By starting with the end in mind, you have a much better chance to be successful.

接下来，定义项目范围、创建工作分解结构。识别你必须满足的质量参数。制定进度。算出需要多少钱。这些要素（范围、质量、工期、成本）是你应监控和控制的基本项，也是你项目计划的基石。一旦把项目拆成可管理的小块，你必须识别最终产品必须具备什么特征才能满足项目质量要求。在你恰当地界定了项目（范围）、记下必须遵守的"规则"（质量）之后，你就能更好地确定完成它需要多久。要算出完成项目需要多少时间，你需要确定每项任务的工期、任务间的依赖、具体约束、以及你可用的资源。成本最后算，因为它通常是你要做的工作、以及完成该工作所需时间和资源的函数。例如，你雇顾问做一项特定任务，他计划做一周和做比如说 10 个月，花费不会相同。最后，考虑采购、沟通和人力资源。以终为始，你成功的概率大得多。

— p.159 —

Clear Terms, Long Friendship!条款清楚，友谊长久！

Matteo Becchi, PMP · Arlington, Virginia, U.S.Matteo Becchi（PMP）· 美国弗吉尼亚州阿灵顿

THE TITLE OF THIS TIP IS FROM AN OLD ITALIAN SAYING: Patti chiari, amicizia lunga, which means "Clear terms equal long friendship." I think this mantra applies to many aspects of project management discipline. On a broader, methodological level, this saying summarizes in my mind the idea behind scope statements, setting goals and deliverables, and creating project definition documents. Really, all project artifacts are geared toward stating upfront the terms and goals the project team is setting out to accomplish. Now take that concept to the 50,000 foot- (or 15,000-meter) view. Look at the initiation and planning phases of the project life cycle across the nine knowledge areas of the PMBOK® Guide, from developing the project charter, scope, work breakdown structure (WBS), schedule, cost estimates, to quality/HR/communication and procurement plans. Each of these activities underlines the heavy focus we dedicate to planning upfront and communicating the plan to all stakeholders to make sure everyone is on the same page. These are basically measures to ensure smooth sailing on the journey that is the project life cycle. Second, on the tactical level, when running meetings make sure you build, or simply state and set, clear project meeting guidelines and expectations with your team, such as: There will be a specific agenda and a required attendees list prepared ahead of time. With the high salary rates of good software developers, you can quickly go over budget if you waste coding time in meetings. Agree that each participant will prepare by gathering information, talking to outside experts, reading relevant publications or research, and consulting old notes or company records, as appropriate. A second meeting with expensive personnel because one teammate did not prepare is inexcusable.

这篇短文的标题来自一句古老意大利谚语：Patti chiari, amicizia lunga，意思是"条款清楚等于友谊长久"。我认为这句箴言适用于项目管理纪律的许多方面。在更宏观的方法论层面，这句话在我脑海中概括了范围说明书、设定目标和交付物、创建项目定义文件背后的理念。真的，所有项目制品都旨在预先说明项目团队着手达成的条款和目标。现在把这个概念拿到 5 万英尺（或 1.5 万米）的高度。看 PMBOK® 指南九大知识领域中项目生命周期的启动和规划阶段：从制定项目章程、范围、工作分解结构（WBS）、进度、成本估算，到质量/人力资源/沟通和采购计划。这些活动每一个都凸显我们对前期规划的高度重视，以及把计划传达给所有相关方、确保大家在同一页上。这些基本上是确保项目生命周期这段航程一帆风顺的措施。第二，在战术层面，开会时确保你和团队建立、或简单陈述并设定清晰的项目会议准则和期望，例如：要有具体议程和必到者名单，提前准备。好软件开发者的薪资很高，如果你在会议里浪费编码时间，预算会很快超支。同意每位参与者都要做准备：收集信息、与外部专家交谈、阅读相关出版物或研究、查阅旧笔记或公司记录（视情况）。因为一个队友没准备而让昂贵人员开第二次会，是不可原谅的。

— p.160 —
  • Arrive at meetings early if you need to plug in a laptop, set up projection equipment, or hook up audio devices for your part of the presentation. If not, come a few minutes early to find a chair, get coffee, and greet other team members.
    如果你需要插笔记本、架投影设备、或为你那部分演示接音频设备，提前到会。如果不需要，也提前几分钟到，找椅子、倒咖啡、问候其他团队成员。
  • Set a "policy" of no communication devices during meetings (BlackBerries, laptops, and cell phones). If you've ever tried to speak while your technically adept software developers text or play games, you know that the programmers are tuning you out.
    定一条会议中不使用通讯设备的「政策」（黑莓、笔记本、手机）。如果你试过在技术娴熟的软件开发者发短信或玩游戏时讲话，你就知道程序员在把你过滤掉。
  • Agree to respect other project team members by refraining from running sidebar conversations, interrupting, or talking over someone who is speaking.
    同意尊重其他项目团队成员，避免私下交谈、打断、或盖过正在发言的人。

Third, create clear contracts with your customers, vendors, and subcontractors. The sales division will focus only on the final product to be delivered and the final price your organization will receive. Be sure it also includes specifics of how changes will be requested and approved, and what the charge for them will be. Try to set a process for how often and in what format the customer expects to be contacted regarding your project. Will your customers be available for questions? Will they be willing to provide end-users to test software features as the development progresses? Clear terms equal long friendships—no matter where in the project environment you look.

第三，与客户、供应商和分包商签订清晰合同。销售部门只关注要交付的最终产品和你组织将收到的最终价格。确保合同还包含变更如何请求、批准、以及如何计费的具体条款。试着定一个流程：客户希望多久被联系一次、以什么格式了解你的项目。客户会有空回答问题吗？他们愿意提供终端用户，在开发过程中测试软件功能吗？条款清楚等于友谊长久——不管你看项目环境的哪个角落。

— p.161 —

The Best Estimators: Those Who Do the Work最好的估算者：做这项工作的人

Joe Zenevitch · New York, New York, U.S.Joe Zenevitch · 美国纽约州纽约市

HAVE YOU BEEN ON A PROJECT where one person creates all the estimates for the work to be done? Has this been a successful approach? My guess is, probably not. There are three major problems with this approach: Unless you are lucky, the developers on the team will not be at the same skill level as the person creating the estimates. So, while the estimates might be accurate if the lead architect were doing all the work, more than likely the developer's pace will vary. The risk that one person estimating for the entire team will be incorrect is pretty high. The more people involved in estimating, the better. Developers are going to be handed an estimate they must meet. Rarely have I seen a developer who is happy with this approach. The worst infraction is when you, as the software project manager, decide you are qualified to provide the estimates for the team. You may think that since you are a former developer you can adequately choose the estimates. Even if you are still actively doing development, think again. The same issues apply as with the lead architect scenario described above, but the longer it's been since you've done active development, the worse your estimates are going to be. And don't even think about estimating if you are leading a team using a technology with which you are unfamiliar. On our projects, we do group estimation using a wideband-delphi approach. We start by having our business analyst describe the requirements for a feature, the development team listens, and then team members ask clarifying questions.

你有没有待过这样的项目：一个人为所有要做的工作做估算？这是成功的做法吗？我猜大概不是。这种做法有三个大问题：除非你运气好，团队开发的技能水平不会和做估算的人一样。所以，虽然如果首席架构师自己做所有工作估算可能准确，但开发的节奏很可能不同。一个人为整个团队做估算出错的风险相当高。参与估算的人越多越好。开发会被塞给一个必须达到的估算。我很少见到开发对这种做法满意。最糟的违规是：你作为软件项目经理，自以为有资格为团队做估算。你可能觉得因为自己以前是开发，就能恰当地做估算。即使你还在积极做开发，再想想。和上面首席架构师场景一样的问题适用，而且你离开实际开发越久，估算越糟。如果你带领的团队用的技术你不熟悉，想都别想做估算。在我们的项目上，我们用宽带德尔菲法做群体估算。开始时业务分析师描述一个功能的需求，开发团队听，然后团队成员问澄清问题。

— p.162 —

Once they are ready to give their initial estimate, they each write their individual figure on a card. When everyone has finished, on the count of three they all hold up their cards. Now we see how they compare. If they are very close, we go with the more conservative number. If there is a wide discrepancy, we ask the developers to talk about the assumptions that went into their estimate. After more discussion, we ask them to estimate again. What happens most frequently is that the estimates converge to a single number as the developers gain a common understanding and agreement on what will be required to complete the feature. This approach is advantageous because: All of the team is involved in coming up with the estimates and all varying perspectives are shared. Often team members are all of one mind and can get to a shared estimate quickly. Later, when actual coding begins, developers have all been exposed to the thought process that went into the estimates, making it less necessary that only certain people can work on any single feature. By having the team "own" the estimate, there is less chance of backlash. Their estimate may still be wrong, but team members will be less confrontational about it and more cooperative in coming to a revised estimate. Remember, the best estimators are those who will do the work.

当他们准备好给出初步估算时，各自把数字写在卡片上。大家写完后，数到三一起举牌。现在看对比。如果很接近，我们取更保守的数字。如果差异大，我们让开发讨论他们估算中的假设。再讨论后，让他们重新估算。最常发生的是：随着开发对完成功能所需条件达成共同理解和一致，估算收敛到一个数字。这种方法有利之处在于：全团队参与估算，各种不同视角都被分享。常常团队成员想法一致，能很快达成共享估算。之后真正编码开始时，开发都接触过做估算时的思考过程，使得"只有某些人能做某个功能"的必要性降低。让团队"拥有"估算，反弹可能性更小。他们的估算可能还是错，但团队成员不会那么对立，而会更合作地修订估算。记住，最好的估算者是将要做这项工作的人。

— p.163 —

Communicating Is Key沟通是关键

Gennady Mironov, CPM · Toronto, Ontario, CanadaGennady Mironov（CPM）· 加拿大安大略省多伦多

THE MOST CRITICAL KNOWLEDGE the project manager in any industry should have is how to be a good communicator. The person may have many different certifications and a list of titles and accreditations after his/her name, but without the basic knowledge of how to collaborate with others, the work of the project cannot be accomplished properly. I strongly believe that when starting a new project, the good project manager should meet in person with all of the stakeholders. Especially the client. The PM should introduce him-/herself and discuss the project goals and all the critical issues. If the stakeholders, client, and even the project team are not located on different continents, meeting in person should not be a big problem, even during an economic recession. We say in Russia that "it's better to see it one time than to hear it a hundred times." From my own project management experience working on multimillion-dollar projects, I've found I could easily solve problems with my clients within half a day by visiting them in person. On one project, we had a problem when our contractor was delaying the project schedule by not supplying us with the required wireless base station. The problem was that the contractor had outsourced this part of the project to its own subcontractor, who was late with the power supply systems. Although we spent weeks of calling and sending numerous emails back and forth, we could not solve this problem. Finally, I chose to meet personally with our contractor, explained the details of the issue, offered some possible solutions, and we were able to get our needed equipment. In most cases, the customer is on your side and ready to support you if you are willing to listen and help come up with a reasonable solution.

任何行业的项目经理最应具备的关键知识，是如何做一个好沟通者。这个人名字后面可能有各种认证、头衔和资质，但不具备与他人协作的基本知识，项目工作就无法妥善完成。我坚信，开始新项目时，好项目经理应与所有相关方当面会面，尤其是客户。项目经理应自我介绍，讨论项目目标和所有关键问题。如果相关方、客户、甚至项目团队不在不同大洲，即使经济衰退期间，当面会面也不该是大问题。我们俄罗斯人说："见一次比听一百次好。"从我自己做数百万美元项目的管理经验看，我发现亲自拜访客户，半天内就能轻松解决问题。有一个项目，我们的承包商延迟了项目进度，因为没有提供所需的无线基站。问题是承包商把这部分外包给了自己的分包商，后者的供电系统延误了。虽然我们花了几周打电话、来回发无数邮件，还是解决不了。最后，我选择亲自见承包商，解释问题细节，提出可能的解决方案，我们终于拿到了需要的设备。大多数情况下，客户站在你这边，只要你愿意倾听并帮忙拿出合理方案，他们就准备支持你。

— p.164 —

Another time, one of our clients insisted on a very short project schedule. He wanted to shorten the production cycle of the equipment at the end of the year, when all the factories were working at 100% capacity to close as many purchase orders as possible. We could not accept this, because it was twice as short as the standard project period. Again, I organized a three-party meeting between our company, the client, and the vendor. We freely proposed the shortest, most realistic schedule, and explained in detail why we couldn't shorten it more. After finishing a specially organized inventory to discover the number of items needed for the project we already had in stock, we took some risk and accepted the customer's order without even receiving the order confirmation from him. We closed the project successfully, two days ahead of that very tight schedule. Our client was very happy, and at the beginning of the new year offered us another unexpected project for another $2 million. We met schedule, scope, budget, and quality requirements, and in this case earned extra profit for the organization as a result of the project. Software projects rest on person-to-person communication.

还有一次，我们一个客户坚持要很短的项目进度。他想在年底缩短设备生产周期，那时所有工厂都 100% 产能运转，以关闭尽可能多的采购订单。我们不能接受，因为它比标准项目周期短一半。我又组织了三方会议：我们公司、客户和供应商。我们坦诚提出最短、最现实的进度，详细解释为什么不能再短。在专门盘点了库存中已有的项目所需物料数量后，我们冒了点风险，甚至没收到客户的订单确认就接受了订单。我们成功收尾项目，比那个极紧的进度还提前两天。客户非常高兴，新年初又给了我们一个意外的 200 万美元项目。我们满足了进度、范围、预算和质量要求，这次还为组织赚了额外利润。软件项目建立在人与人的沟通之上。

— p.165 —

A Project Is the Pursuit of a Solution项目是对解决方案的追求

Cynthia A. Berg, PhD (ABD), PMP · Glendale, Arizona, U.S.Cynthia A. Berg（PhD ABD, PMP）· 美国亚利桑那州格伦代尔

AUTHOR STEPHEN COVEY STATES, "BEGIN WITH THE END IN MIND." And what is a project, except the pursuit of an end solution? The best way to conceptualize the end of a software project is to create a work breakdown structure (WBS). The WBS is a hierarchical view, which shows the entire scope of the project broken down into deliverables, much like an organizational chart shows company divisions broken into departments and then work teams. The deliverables are then divided into smaller and smaller components until they get to the work package level. Include the team, sponsors, and other stakeholders when creating a WBS. This ensures that the work of the project is fully defined and represents the needs of all of the participants. Why include the team? Well, who knows the work that needs to be done better than the project team members who will actually do those tasks? Projects are doomed to fail when the project manager assumes that he/she alone knows how to list every facet of the work of the project. While creating a WBS, the team has an opportunity to challenge the norms of "how we've always done it." Plus, team members are formulating a shared opinion on what constitutes the work of the project. This method ensures that they will have more buy-in for the effort. After all, it's always more interesting to work on a project you helped to design.

作家 Stephen Covey 说："以终为始。"项目是什么？不就是对一个最终解决方案的追求吗？概念化软件项目结尾的最好办法，是创建工作分解结构（WBS）。WBS 是层级视图，显示项目整个范围被拆成交付物，很像组织架构图显示公司分部被拆成部门、再拆成工作团队。交付物再被分成越来越小的组件，直到工作包层级。创建 WBS 时让团队、发起人和其他相关方参与。这确保项目工作被完整定义，并代表所有参与者的需要。为什么包括团队？谁比真正要做这些任务的项目团队成员更知道需要做什么工作？当项目经理自以为只有自己知道如何列出项目工作的每一个方面时，项目注定失败。创建 WBS 时，团队有机会挑战"我们一直就是这么做的"惯例。而且，团队成员正在就什么构成项目工作形成共同意见。这种方法确保他们对这份努力有更多认同。毕竟，做一个你帮忙设计的项目总是更有趣。

* Deliverable: A product, result, or capability to perform a service that is created through the work of a project.* 交付物：通过项目工作创造的产品、结果、或执行一项服务的能力。

† Work package: The smallest portion of a deliverable, including activities and schedule milestones. The goal is to be able to assign it to one person, group, or vendor.† 工作包：交付物的最小部分，包括活动和进度里程碑。目标是能把它指派给一个人、一个群体或一个供应商。

— p.166 —

How small should the activities of the WBS be broken down? That's a trick question. There are no activities shown in the WBS, since it is only divided to the work package level. Once that work package is assigned to the department, group, vendor, or subcontractor who will complete it, it can be broken down further into the activities and milestones necessary to ensure that it is done efficiently and with quality processes. Each assignee for a work package, the lowest level of work, should create his or her own smaller project plan portion that will flow back into the master schedule. The WBS then becomes the backbone for all other planning, executing, monitoring, and controlling functions within the project. It also serves as a succinct communication tool for those both internal and external to the project. A graphic representation of a WBS is a picture of the project solution. Once that picture is completed, the detailed planning, scheduling, and budgeting can begin. How can you plan, budget, and schedule before you have clearly defined the work of the project? The WBS is also invaluable as a brainstorming tool. With a graphic representation that displays the entirety of the project, it's easy to spot omissions, redundancies, or fertile pockets of work that could easily be enhanced to leverage the value of the project. To identify potential risks (both internal and external), look at each portion of the WBS. A little time up front to get a clear work breakdown structure that is prepared, understood, and agreed upon among all stakeholders is a recipe for project excellence.

WBS 的活动应该拆到多小？这是个陷阱问题。WBS 里没有活动，因为它只分解到工作包层级。一旦工作包被指派给将完成它的部门、群体、供应商或分包商，它可以进一步分解为确保高效、有质量流程完成所需的活动和里程碑。每个工作包（最低工作层级）的承担者应创建自己更小的项目计划部分，回流到主进度。WBS 于是成为项目中所有其他规划、执行、监控和控制职能的主干。它也作为项目内外人员的简洁沟通工具。WBS 的图形表示就是项目解决方案的图。这张图完成后，详细规划、进度和预算才能开始。在你清晰定义项目工作之前，你怎么规划、预算和排进度？WBS 作为头脑风暴工具也极有价值。有了显示项目整体的图形表示，很容易发现遗漏、冗余、或容易被增强以杠杆化项目价值的肥沃工作块。要识别潜在风险（内部和外部），看 WBS 的每个部分。前期花一点时间，得到一个所有相关方都准备好、理解并同意的清晰工作分解结构，是项目卓越的秘诀。
